title: Validation of a stability-indicating HPLC-UV method for the quantification of acetazolamide in Oral-Mix and Oral-Mix SF
author: Gillium, Friciu, et al.

steps.title: Prepare acetazolamide suspension
steps.instruction: Weigh acetazolamide bulk powder and mix with Oral Mix or Oral Mix SF in a mortar using a pestle to obtain a homogeneous suspension at 25 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC injection solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the suspension and process the aliquots to obtain a 100 µg mL⁻¹ solution ready for immediate HPLC analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL of the 25 mg mL⁻¹ acetazolamide suspension into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube and add 450 µL methanol.
Pipette 20 µL of the clear supernatant into a new tube and add 480 µL mobile phase A.
Transfer the final solution to a sealed 96‑well plate; the solution now has a nominal concentration of 100 µg mL⁻¹ and should be analyzed immediately.

description: In order to define the validation parameters of this method, including (1) Linearity and range, (2) accuracy, (3) precision and (4) specificity, several reports and guidelines pertaining to the validation of stability-indicating HPLC methods were considered [7], [8], [9], [10], [11], [12], [13], [14], [15]. Limits of detection and quantification were not formally evaluated as the lower concentration of the validation range was clearly above the limit of quantification based on signal to noise ratio. This method is not intended to be used outside of its validated range. Since robustness was not evaluated, this method requires calibration i. Furthermore, the injection of quality control samples every 20 test samples will confirm the stability of the system throughout injection runs. This stability check was applied when assessing the stability of acetazolamide oral suspensions over a period of 90 days.
